title: $f^!$ with finite coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an arbitrary field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting; def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $A$ be any finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, given the discrete topology, and write $\underline A$ for its condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For each such scheme $T$, identify the pulled-back ring object $p_T^*\underline A$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] with the constant ring sheaf $A_T$. Use the section-action equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to identify internal $p_T^*\underline A$-module objects with ordinary $A_T$-module sheaves, and its termwise derived equivalence to identify their derived categories. Under this exact, tensor-compatible equivalence, write $\Dctf(T,A)$ for the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory: the module-object definition is [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and its ordinary-module form is [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf; def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Let $\Loc(\Dctf(T,A))$ be the full triangulated closure under arbitrary small sums of [sk-def-localizing-closure], identified by that same equivalence. Let
$$f^!: \Loc(\Dctf(Y,A))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$$
be the right adjoint to $Rf_!$ of [sk-prop-sf-existence], with both functors viewed in these identified categories. Then
$$f^!\bigl(\Dctf(Y,A)\bigr)\subseteq\Dctf(X,A).$$
Consequently this adjunction restricts to
$$Rf_!: \Dctf(X,A)\ \rightleftarrows\ \Dctf(Y,A):f^!.$$
For smooth $f$ of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], its restriction is étale locally on $X$ naturally isomorphic to $f^*(-)(d)[2d]$. Here choose $N=\ell^r\geq1$ annihilating $A$ and define the pro-étale twist $A_T(d)$ to be $\nu_T^*$ of the ordinary étale twist of [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], using the exact site-comparison pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]; $(-)(d)$ means derived tensor with this line. The canonical global isomorphism is constructed separately in the smooth-purity chapter.

proof.text: Work on ordinary étale sites. Finite-type $k$-schemes and their opens are Noetherian and quasi-separated; the opens are quasi-compact finite-type morphisms, separated since their diagonals are identities. Nagata and the ambient theorem give the required adjoints. Fix invertible $N=\ell^r$ annihilating $A$.

For closed $i$ with complement $j$, relative finite cohomological dimension gives $R^qj_*M=0$ for $q>e$ for every module sheaf, using the forgetful comparison and $NM=0$. Constructibility and closed amplitude give $i^\times K$ constructible interval $[r,s+e+1]$. Closed $i$ is finite proper with exact $i_*$, so its identity/proper compactification gives $Ri_!=i_*$ and the support adjoint.

The stalk test gives $j^*K$ Tor interval $[a,b]$. Finite $A$ is Noetherian and finite modules are finitely presented: kernels of finite free presentations are finite. The finite-constant projection lemma and open Tor lemma give $Rj_*j^*K$ interval $[a,b+e]$. The support triangle and support Tor lemma, with exact $i^*$ and $i^*i_*\simeq1$, give $i^\times K$ interval $[a,b+e+1]$.

For smooth $p$ of dimension $m$, the tensor formula gives $p^\times K=p^*K\otimes L[2m]$, with $L$ locally free of rank one. Exact constructible pullback and the stalk Tor test preserve intervals; locally tensoring with $L$ is the identity. Shifting subtracts $2m$ from both endpoints. Hence smooth $p^\times$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$.

Take the finite charts $fs=vpi$ from the gluing lemma. By steps 2–4, $B=i^\times p^\times v^*K$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor. Evaluate the chart Hom bijection at $H=B$ and $1_B$ to obtain $\alpha:B\to s^*f^\times K$. Naturality in $H$ identifies postcomposition with $\alpha$ with those bijections, including every shift. The bounded-below Hom test makes $\alpha$ invertible; finite-cover gluing proves ordinary preservation. Naturality in $K$ follows by testing the comparison square out of $B$ and using injectivity.

source.place: Opening and final paragraphs: charts and gluing

proof.text: The coefficient equivalence and exceptional transport supply $H_K\in\Dctf(X,A)$ and $t_K:Rf_!H_K\to K$ with bijective Hom maps on bounded-below étale-origin objects. Each generator and shift has such origin. Transpose $t_K$ to $\alpha:H_K\to f^!K$. Its maps on shifted-generator Hom sets are those bijections. Both objects belong to the localizing closure, so the localizing Hom test makes $\alpha$ invertible, naturally in $K$.

source.place: Closed-adjoint uniqueness and final restriction paragraphs

proof.text: Forward compact-support preservation and the result above restrict the given Hom bijections to the full $\Dctf$ subcategories. For smooth $f$, trivialize both the smooth tensor line $L$ and $A_X(d)$ on a common étale refinement. There $L\simeq A_X(d)$ naturally yields $f^*(-)(d)[2d]$. Transport along $\nu^*$ using tensor/pullback comparison and step 6. This asserts only an étale-local formula.

Base steps 2–4, 7, 8, 10 and 11 stay as short steps assembling dedicated existing nodes: lem-exc-closed-amplitude with lem-kun-0f10(1), the forget comparison and thm-dg; projection-finite-constant, open-tor-bound and closed-support-tor-bound; thm-asd-smooth-tensor; the gluing node; the exceptional transport; det-ctf clause (3). What was cut from those steps is hypothesis checking, not hidden arguments. All four new statements are true and I tested them on small cases: the stalk test through the point-topos tensor pullback and conservativity, with K=A at a point and A=0; the brutal-tail telescope via lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim; the orthogonality argument on Loc, with S empty; the chart Hom chain composing only on D^+, with identity charts and empty U. None is a duplicate: I compared them with lem-sfb-etale-derived-tensor-stalk, lem-sf-open-tor-bound-arbitrary-field, lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology, lem-sc-compact-generator-ambient-thick, lem-sc-perfect-localizing-iso-locus, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality and lem-etale-exceptional-locality-arbitrary-schemes. The parent assembly is valid: in step 5, Yoneda at H=B gives α=φ_B(1_B) and postcomposition matches every shift; in step 6, the generators have D^b étale origin and the Hom map is h↦t_K∘Rf_!h; both H_K and f^!K lie in Loc. No SGA is used, the item is not dropped, and there are no cycles. All split_report.tool_uses are used generic inputs inherited from the base PASS, and I accept them. No fixes.
